chapter_title: Day 9, Part 2: Venetian Heraklion and Crete Today
learning_objective: The learner will locate eight landmarks of Venetian and Ottoman Heraklion on a street map of the old town, placing at least six of the eight within 150 m of the true position on the first attempt.

Type: map **sim-id:** walking-venetian-candia-map
**Library:** Leaflet
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** locate
**Learning Objective:** The learner will locate eight landmarks of Venetian and Ottoman Heraklion on a street map of the old town, placing at least six of the eight within 150 m of the true position on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Candia, the Morosini Fountain, the Loggia, the Church of Agios Titos, the Venetian arsenal, Koules Fortress, the Venetian walls and bastions, the Martinengo Bastion, and the Pantocrator (Chania) Gate (all defined in Part One above), and the Heraklion Archaeological Museum (Chapter 13). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of eight landmark cards, the learner clicks the map where they think the landmark stands. A placement is correct when the click is within 150 m of the landmark's reference point. Mastery is 6 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Panning, zooming, and opening infoboxes after an answer are exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The Koules stands on the shore of the town rather than out at the end of the harbor breakwater (card 5). (2) The Venetian walls run along the harbor, when they enclose the town on its landward side (cards 7 and 8). (3) The landmarks are spread across the city, when the Venetian civic center (fountain, Loggia, Agios Titos) lies within about 200 m. **Instructional Rationale:** Locating a landmark from a description is the Remember-level skill a walker needs before arriving; committing a click before the answer appears turns a glance at a map into retrieval practice. Revealing each landmark's era and date in its infobox ties the location to the layer it belongs to. **Content:** A street map of Heraklion's old town, centered on 35.3385, 25.1330, at a zoom that shows the whole area inside the walls and the harbor breakwater. Landmark names are not labeled on the map until answered. Cards, in this order: | # | Card shown to the learner | Reference point (lat, lon) | Infobox shown after answering | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Lions Square: the Morosini Fountain and the Basilica of San Marco | 35.3392, 25.1334 | Venetian. Fountain built 1628 by the governor Francesco Morosini; San Marco first built in the 13th century, later a mosque, now an exhibition hall. | | 2 | The Loggia, meeting hall of the Venetian nobility | 35.3399, 25.1340 | Venetian, built in the 1620s; damaged in the Second World War and restored; now part of city hall. | | 3 | The Church of Agios Titos | 35.3401, 25.1349 | Byzantine foundation after 961; Catholic under Venice; a mosque under the Ottomans, rebuilt after the 1856 earthquake; an Orthodox church again from 1925. Holds the relic of Titus, returned from Venice in 1966. | | 4 | The Venetian arsenal, the galley sheds | 35.3422, 25.1353 | Venetian state shipyard: vaulted sheds where galleys were built and stored. | | 5 | Koules Fortress, the Venetian sea fortress | 35.3444, 25.1369 | Venetian *Rocca a Mare*, built 1523–1540 at the end of the harbor breakwater; named Koules ("tower") by the Ottomans. | | 6 | The Heraklion Archaeological Museum | 35.3389, 25.1375 | Modern museum (1937–1940) of Minoan Crete; where our Day 9 began (Chapter 13). | | 7 | The Martinengo Bastion and the grave of Nikos Kazantzakis | 35.3317, 25.1311 | Venetian bastion, the southernmost of seven; Kazantzakis (1883–1957) is buried on top. | | 8 | The Pantocrator Gate, also called the Chania Gate | 35.3378, 25.1255 | Venetian gate in the western walls, on the road to Chania. | After card 8 the map shows all eight markers and a line along our own walk on Day 9: Archaeological Museum, Lions Square, Loggia, Agios Titos, arsenal, Koules. **Provenance:** Landmark descriptions and dates from Part One of this chapter and from Chapter 13. Reference points for cards 1 to 4 are rounded from the locations of our own photos taken at those places on Day 9; card 5 is rounded from the Wikipedia article "Koules Fortress"; card 6 is the value in `data/chapter-places.json`; cards 7 and 8 are approximate. Before publishing, the generator must check every reference point against OpenStreetMap and correct any that is more than 50 m from the landmark, and note the correction in the sim's index page. **Rules:** Distance is great-circle (haversine) distance in meters from the click to the reference point. A placement is correct if distance <= 150 m. Each card allows two attempts; only the first counts toward the score. After a second miss, the marker appears at the reference point. Score is 0 to 8; mastery is score >= 6 on first attempts. Zoom uses the map's buttons, not the mouse wheel. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads card 1 and clicks the map where the landmark stands. 2. The sim draws the click, the true marker, and the distance in meters, and opens the infobox. 3. The learner moves to the next card; answered markers stay visible. 4. After card 8 the walking line appears, and the learner should notice that cards 1 to 5 lie on one short downhill route to the sea, while the walls (cards 7 and 8) ring the town's upper edge. **Feedback:** Eight cards, fixed order. Correct: "Correct: [distance] m away. [Infobox text]". First miss: "Not quite: [distance] m away. Try again." The miss message for card 5 adds "Look out along the harbor breakwater."; for cards 7 and 8 it adds "The walls ring the town on its landward side." Second miss: "Here it is." and the marker and infobox appear. At the end: "First-attempt score: n of 8." If n >= 6: "You could walk Venetian Candia without a map." Otherwise: "Try again, starting from the Lions." A Try Again option resets all cards. **Starting State:** The unlabeled street map of the old town and card 1, with the question "Where would you find the Lions?" **Chapter Anchors:** Morosini Fountain 1628; Koules built 1523–1540; seven bastions; Martinengo the southernmost; Agios Titos an Orthodox church again from 1925, relic returned 1966; from the Lions to the Koules is less than a kilometer, all downhill; eight landmarks; mastery 6 of 8.
